sentences.text: It is a case of injury.
The contention of the claimant is that it is a head on collision and the injured has suffered 30% partial and permanent disability and the is not able to walk.
Therefore, the compensation granted under the head of pain and suffering ought to be increased.
It is seen that the Tribunal has fixed for pain and suffering for a sum of Rs.35,000/- and for loss of convenience is Rs.25,000/-.
Since the injured is not able to walk until now, this Court is inclined to grant a sum of Rs.70,000/- under the head of pain and suffering.
As far as loss of convenience is concerned this Court is granting a sum of Rs.50,000/-.
The compensation granted under the other heads are confirmed.

3. Accordingly, the claimant is entitled for compensation as follows:

Therefore, this Court is inclined to enhance a sum of Rs.6,23,015/-from Rs.5,63,015, as compensation.
4. In view of the said modification, these Civil Miscellaneous Appeals are disposed of.

The award amount of Rs.5,63,015/- granted by the Tribunal is enhanced to Rs.6,23,015/- and the respondents in C.M.A(MD) No. 1141 of 2021 is directed to deposit the same with 7.5% interest along with costs,
within a period of Twelve weeks, from the date of receipt of copy of the order, less the amount if already deposited.
On such deposing being made, the claimant is permitted to withdraw the same.
The claimant is directed to pay the deficit Court fee for the enhanced compensation.
No costs.
Consequently, connected miscellaneous petition is closed.
